newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends firm on strong cargo trade, crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends firm on strong cargo trade, crude.

text.p: NWE naphtha ended with strong gains after a sharp rebound in crude oil futures and a cargo deal nearly $3 higher than on Tuesday, traders and brokers said.
An Egyptian Alex cargo traded at $186.75 cif basis Rotterdam to arrive June 16, they said. The last deal heard done was for light virgin naphtha at $184 cif on Tuesday.
June swaps, in response, rose $2.50 to $181/$183 a tonne and its backwardation widened to $2 versus July, which was valued at $179/$180.
"There is one school of thought which is the market is overvalued and needs to go down," said one.
"In the real market, to buy a cargo, it is very, very thin."

He also cooled off arguments that the sharp drop in gasoline prices meant demand for heavier naphthenic and aromatic (N+A) was drying up. Some reformer demand was still needed to make hydrogen, he said.
N+A material is a feedstock for making gasoline.
"There is still not much quality N+A around," he said.
NYMEX gasoline futures also rebounded more than one cent a gallon, recovering from a 2.50 cent selloff on Tuesday, despite U.S. inventory data showing a healthy increase in supplies last week.
